reasons: The inserted Section 14.2A supplies every atomic element of the fallback: Vendor retains generic tools and know-how, and Customer gets a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables for its business.

Preferred is not met because Vendor's exclusive ownership of Deliverables and the absence of any assignment remain, and Customer Data rights are not addressed here — but the locked target is fallback.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion rather than a rewrite of Section 14.2, and it expressly disapplies only the conflicting revocable, non-transferable and Order Form term limitations, avoiding contradiction.
No unrelated term is disturbed; Section 14.3's Vendor Technology retention, identification duty and third-party material restriction remain effective, and no undefined term is introduced.
